checks: No eclipse at 1 of 14 covered epochs where the 1.82052 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 178331798 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.8205 days. Automated analysis of TESS photometry detected a primary eclipse causing a 2.45% dimming of starlight, with a strong signal-to-noise ratio of 79.9 from the box-least-squares search algorithm. No secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level image analysis provided a difference-imaging confirmation with a signal-to-noise peak of 7.9, though the centroid offset measured 9.0 arcsec from the target. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously unlisted object. The machine-learning screening score of 0.35 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a real stellar target. This candidate has passed all automated data quality checks.
